questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The correct sequence of adult cell cycle phases is __________.
questions.solution:
The cell cycle is divided into two basic phases: Interphase and M Phase (Mitosis phase).

Interphase is further divided into three phases:
G1 phase (Gap 1): The cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA.
S phase (Synthesis): DNA replication takes place.
G2 phase (Gap 2): Proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.

Following interphase, the cell enters the M phase where actual cell division occurs.

Therefore, the correct sequence of the cell cycle phases is G1-S-G2-M.

options: Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false
questions.solution:
According to the NCERT, diakinesis is the final stage of meiotic prophase I. During this phase, the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled to prepare the homologous chromosomes for separation. Thus, Statement I is correct.

Meiosis II is initiated immediately after cytokinesis. In contrast to meiosis I, meiosis II resembles a normal mitosis because it involves the separation of sister chromatids. Meiosis I is a reductional division where homologous chromosomes separate. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

Answer: Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false

questions.solution:
The cell cycle is divided into two basic phases: 
a. Interphase: The phase between subsequent cell divisions is called the interphase. The interphase lasts for more than 95% of the cell cycle. The interphase is further divided into three stages, i.e. G1, S and G2.
b. M Phase (Mitotic phase): The actual cell division takes place in the M-phase. The M-phase lasts for less than 5% of the cell cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During meiosis <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><mo>,</mo></math> in which stage synapsis takes place?
questions.solution:
Prophase I is subdivided into five phases, viz. Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene and Diakinesis. 

Leptotene: During this stage, the chromosomes become gradually visible under a light microscope. Compaction of chromosomes continues throughout this phase. 

Zygotene: Chromosomes start pairing together. This process is called synapsis. The paired chromosomes are called homologous chromosomes. The formation of synapsis is accompanied by the formation of the synaptonemal complex. 

Pachytene: Recombination nodules appear. These nodules are the sites at which crossing over takes place between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes. 
 
Diplotene: Synapotnemal complex is dissolved at this stage. The recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalent separate from each other; except at the site of crossing over. The X-shaped structures; thus formed; are called chiasmata. 

Diakinesis: Chiasmata is terminated at this stage.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the following with respect to meiosis

(a) Zygotene (i) Terminalization
(b) Pachytene (ii) Chiasmata
(c) Diplotene (iii) Crossing over
(d) Diakinesis (iv) Synapsis

Select the correct option from the following
questions.solution:
Prophase I: 
Prophase in meiosis-I is typically longer and more complex than the prophase in meiosis II. Prophase I is subdivided into five phases, viz. Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene and Diakinesis. 

Leptotene: 
• During this stage, the chromosomes become gradually visible under the light microscope. The compaction of chromosomes continues throughout this phase. 

Zygotene: 
• Chromosomes start pairing together. This process is called synapsis. The paired chromosomes are called homologous chromosomes. 
• Formation of synapsis is accompanied by the formation of the synaptonemal complex. 
• The synaptonemal complex by a pair of homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent or a tetrad. 

Pachytene: 
• Bivalent chromosomes clearly appear as tetrads, at this stage. 
• Recombination nodules appear. These nodules are the sites at which crossing overtakes place between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes. 
• Exchange of genetic materials between two homologous chromosomes takes place during crossing over. This leads to the recombination of genetic materials on the two chromosomes. 

Diplotene: 
• Synapotnemal complex is dissolved at this stage. 
• The recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalent separate from each other; except at the site of crossing over. 
• The X-shaped structures; thus formed; are called chiasmata. 

Diakinesis: 
• Chiasmata is terminated at this stage. 
• Meiotic spindles are formed to prepare the homologous chromosomes for separation. 
• Nucleolus disappears and nuclear envelope breaks down by the end of diakinesis.

options: Reorganisation of all cell components takes place.
Cell is metabolically active, grows but does not replicate its DNA.
DNA synthesis or replication takes place.
questions.solution: G1 Phase: G1 phase is the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication. In this phase, the cell does not synthesize or, replicate DNA but remains metabolically active. The cell grows in size continuously and synthesizes nucleotides, ATP, proteins, amino acids, RNAs etc. (required during S phase). The length of the G1 phase varies from one cell to another. If a cell divides frequently, then it has a shorter G1 phase and if a cell does not divide frequently, then it has a longer G1 phase. Replication of DNA and duplication of histones takes place in S phase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select the correct statements.

A. Tetrad formation is seen during the Leptotene.

B. During Anaphase, the centromeres split and chromatids separate.

C. Terminalization takes place during Pachytene.

D. Nucleolus, Golgi complex and ER are reformed during Telophase.

E. Crossing over takes place between sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Tetrad formation occurs during the zygotene stage of meiotic prophase. Hence, statement A is not correct.

Anaphase stage is characterised by the following key events:

  • Centromeres split and chromatids separate.
  • Chromatids move to opposite poles.

Hence, statement B is correct.

Terminalisation of chiasma occurs during diplotene, after crossing over at pachytene, and terminalisation completion takes place in diakinesis. Hence, statement C is not correct.

During telophase, the nucleolus, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and Golgi apparatus reappear. Hence, statement D is correct.

Crossing over is the exchange of chromosomal segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during the production of gametes. Hence, statement E is not correct.

Hence, option C is correct, i.e, statement B and D is correct.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The correct sequence of phases of cell cycle is:
questions.solution:
Interphase accounts for almost 95% of the total time required for the cell cycle. Interphase takes place in three stages; G1, S and G2 proceeded by mitotic phase (M phase) and cytokinesis. The nuclear content of DNA is duplicated during the synthesis phase. So, the correct sequence is -

G1→S→G2→M

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cells in G<sub>0</sub> phase:
questions.solution:
• The cells remain in an inert state in the G0 phase of the cell cycle. Hence, G0 can be either viewed as the distinct inert stage which occurs outside the cell cycle or as an extension to the G1 phase, where cell neither divides nor prepares for it.
  • Sometimes, G0 is also referred to as “post-mitotic” state where cells in G0 are in non-dividing phase in the outside of cell cycle.
  • Some types of cells, such as nerve and heart muscle cells, become post-mitotic when they reach maturity (i.e., when they are terminally differentiated) but continue to perform their main functions for the rest of the organism's life.
  • Multinucleated muscle cells which don’t undergo cytokinesis are also thought to be in the G0 stage. Hence, it suspends the cell cycle.
  • G0 stage represents actually indicates the arrest of cell cycle and onset of differentiation.

condensation  <math><mo>→</mo></math>  crossing over  <math><mo>→</mo></math>  nuclear membrane disassembly  <math><mo>→</mo></math>  segregation  <math><mo>→</mo></math>  telophase

The correct sequence of events during mitosis would be as follows

(i) Condensation of DNA so that chromosomes become visible occurs during early to mid-prophase.

(ii) Nuclear membrane disassembly begins at late prophase or transition to metaphase.

(iii) An arrangement of chromosomes at equator occurs during metaphase, called congression.

(iv) Centromere division or splitting occurs during anaphase forming daughter chromosomes.

(v) Segregation also occurs during anaphase as daughter chromosomes separate and move to opposite poles.

(vi) Telophase leads to the formation of two daughter nuclei.

questions.solution:
Zygotene: 

  • Chromosomes start pairing together. This process is called synapsis. The paired chromosomes are called homologous chromosomes. 
  • The formation of synapsis is accompanied by the formation of the synaptonemal complex. 
  • The synaptonemal complex by a pair of homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent or a tetrad.

Pachytene: 

  • Bivalent chromosomes clearly appear as tetrads, at this stage. 
  • Recombination nodules appear. These nodules are the sites at which crossing overtakes place between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes.

  • The nucleolus disappears and the nuclear envelope breaks down by the end of diakinesis.

  • Spindle fibres from opposite poles attach to the pair of homologous chromosomes.

A typical cell cycle comprises two major phases:

  1. Interphase, which is the largest phase of the cell cycle (nearly 95%) and is the most active phase, biochemically, and physiologically.
  2. Division phase, in which the cell actually divides to form the daughter cells.

questions.solution:
Explanation for the correct option:
1. At certain points during M-phase, both \(4 C\) and \(2 C\) DNA is present.
2. The S phase occurs when the amount of DNA in the cell doubles.
3. As a result, the amount of DNA present in the \(G 2\) phase is 4 C.
4. The cell's contents have been doubled, preparing it for further mitotic division.
5. Interphase is made up of the G1 phase (cell growth). S phase (DNA synthesis), and G2 phase (cell growth).
6. At the completion of the interphase, the mitotic phase begins, which consists of mitosis and cytokinesis and results in the production of two daughter cells.
Explanation for the incorrect option:
Option A:
1. The RNA, proteins and other macromolecules essential for the multiplication of cell organelles, spindle formation, and cell development are created during the G2 phase (Gap 2) as the cell prepares to enter the mitotic phase.
2. The G2 phase is characterized by fast cell growth and protein synthesis as the cell prepares for mitosis.
3. Surprisingly, the G2 phase is not required for all cell types, since some (especially immature Xenopus embryos and certain malignancies) progress directly from DNA replication to mitosis.
Option B:
1. During the G1 phase, the cell physically expands and increases the volume of both protein and organelles.
2. During the S phase, the cell duplicates its nucleosomes and copies its DNA to form two sister chromatids.
3. The G1/S transition is a step in the cell cycle that occurs at the junction of the G1 phase, during which the cell develops, and the S phase, during which DNA is reproduced.
Option C:
1. GO phase: resting state, also known as the gap phase.
2. Many cells spend the majority of their time in this phase, either resting or executing assigned tasks.
3. Chemotherapy is generally ineffective. G1 phase: gap 1 phase, also known as interphase.
Final answer: G2 and M phase(s) of the cell cycle, the amount of DNA in a cell remains at 4C level if the initial amount is denoted as 2C.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the starting point of all living organisms?
questions.solution: Are you aware that all organisms, even the largest, start their life from a single cell? You may wonder how a single cell then goes on to form such large organisms. Growth and reproduction are characteristics of cells, indeed of all living organisms. All cells reproduce by dividing into two, with each parental cell giving rise to two daughter cells each time they divide. These newly formed daughter cells can themselves grow and divide, giving rise to a new cell population that is formed by the growth and division of a single parental cell and its progeny. In other words, such cycles of growth and division allow a single cell to form a structure consisting of millions of cells.

questions.q: What is the main process that occurs during cell division?
questions.solution: Cell division is a very important process in all living organisms. During the division of a cell, DNA replication and cell growth also take place. All these processes, i.e., cell division, DNA replication, and cell growth, hence, have to take place in a coordinated way to ensure correct division and formation of progeny cells containing intact genomes. The sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises the other constituents of the cell and eventually divides into two daughter cells is termed cell cycle. Although cell growth (in terms of cytoplasmic increase) is a continuous process, DNA synthesis occurs only during one specific stage in the cell cycle. The replicated chromosomes (DNA) are then distributed to daughter nuclei by a complex series of events during cell division.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Interphase is called the resting phase, during which the cell prepares for division by undergoing cell growth and DNA replication in an orderly manner.
Reason (R): The orderly sequence of phases in interphase is $\text{G}_{1} \rightarrow \text{G}_{2} \rightarrow \text{S}$, ensuring that DNA is replicated just before mitosis begins.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the interphase, though called the resting phase, is the time during which the cell prepares for division by undergoing both cell growth and DNA replication in an orderly manner. Thus, Assertion (A) is correct.

The correct chronological sequence of interphase is $\text{G}_{1} \rightarrow \text{S} \rightarrow \text{G}_{2}$. The Reason statement incorrectly places the $\text{G}_{2}$ phase before the Synthesis ($\text{S}$) phase. Therefore, Reason (R) is not correct.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A cytologist observes a meiotic cell in which the enzyme recombinase is highly active, facilitating the exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids. Identify the current stage of this cell and the defining event that will mark the beginning of the immediately following stage.
options:
Current stage: Pachytene
Event of next stage: Formation of the synaptonemal complex

Current stage: Zygotene
Event of next stage: Appearance of recombination nodules

Current stage: Diplotene
Event of next stage: Terminalisation of chiasmata

Current stage: Pachytene
Event of next stage: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex
questions.solution:
The high activity of the enzyme recombinase and the active exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids indicate that the cell is currently in the pachytene stage of prophase I.

The stage immediately following pachytene is diplotene. According to NCERT, the beginning of the diplotene stage is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes to separate, revealing X-shaped structures called chiasmata.

Formation of the synaptonemal complex occurs earlier, during zygotene. Terminalisation of chiasmata marks diakinesis, which is the stage that follows diplotene.

Answer: Current stage: Pachytene
Event of next stage: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Read the following statements regarding cell division and choose the incorrect statement.
options: Kinetochores are small disc-shaped structures present at the surface of the centromeres.
During mitotic metaphase, spindle fibres attach to the kinetochores of chromosomes.
During metaphase I of meiosis, the bivalent chromosomes align on the equatorial plate.
During metaphase I of meiosis, microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle attach to the kinetochores of sister chromatids.
questions.solution:
The statement in option 4 is incorrect. During metaphase I of meiosis, the microtubules from the opposite poles of the spindle attach to the kinetochores of homologous chromosomes, not sister chromatids. The sister chromatids remain attached at their centromeres and move to the same pole during anaphase I.

Options 1, 2, and 3 are factually correct statements as per NCERT descriptions of mitosis and meiosis I.

Answer: During metaphase I of meiosis, microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle attach to the kinetochores of sister chromatids.

questions.subject: Botany

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:

Kinetochores are small disc-shaped structures present on the surface of the centromere, which serve as the attachment sites for spindle fibres.

The centromere is the primary constriction of a chromosome that holds two sister chromatids together.

The centrosome is an organelle containing two centrioles that radiates out microtubular aster rays during prophase to form the mitotic apparatus.

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
A.Prophasei.Centromeres split and chromatids separate

C.Anaphaseiii.Initiation of the assembly of mitotic spindle
D.Telophaseiv.Spindle fibres attach to kinetochores of chromosomes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The correct matching of the stages of mitosis with their defining events is as follows:

Prophase (A) is characterised by the initiation of the assembly of the mitotic spindle (iii).

Metaphase (B) is defined by the alignment of chromosomes at the equator and the attachment of spindle fibres to the kinetochores of chromosomes (iv).

Anaphase (C) is marked by the splitting of centromeres and the separation of chromatids, which then move to opposite poles (i).

Telophase (D) is the final stage where chromosomes cluster at opposite spindle poles and lose their discrete identity as the nuclear envelope reforms (ii).

Therefore, the correct matching code is A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

Answer: A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): After Meiosis I, the chromosome number is reduced to half, but each chromosome still contains two sister chromatids.
Reason (R): During Anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate but the centromere of each chromosome does not split.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because Meiosis I is a reductional division where the chromosome number is halved. However, the chromosomes at the end of Meiosis I (in each of the two daughter cells) are present as dyads, meaning each still consists of two sister chromatids.

Reason (R) is also correct and provides the correct explanation for (A). During Anaphase I, the homologous chromosomes separate and move to opposite poles, but the centromeres holding the sister chromatids together do not split. Because the centromeres remain intact, the sister chromatids do not separate until Anaphase II. This is exactly why each chromosome still has two chromatids after Meiosis I.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A cell at the $G_{1}$ phase of its cell cycle has 14 chromosomes and 20 pg of DNA. What will be the number of chromosomes and the amount of DNA in the same cell at the $G_{2}$ phase?
questions.solution:
During the cell cycle, the $G_{1}$ phase is followed by the S phase and then the $G_{2}$ phase.

In the S (synthesis) phase, DNA replication occurs. As a result, the amount of DNA per cell doubles. Therefore, the initial 20 pg of DNA in the $G_{1}$ phase will become 40 pg by the $G_{2}$ phase.

However, during the S phase, there is no increase in the chromosome number because the newly synthesized sister chromatids remain attached at the same centromere. Thus, the cell will still have 14 chromosomes in the $G_{2}$ phase.

Hence, the cell at the $G_{2}$ phase will have 14 chromosomes and 40 pg of DNA.

Answer: 14 chromosomes and 40 pg of DNA

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In adult animals, some cells like heart cells do not appear to exhibit division. Which specific cell cycle transition do these cells undergo to reach this non-dividing state?
options: They exit $\mathrm{G}_1$ phase to enter an inactive stage called $\mathrm{G}_0$.
They exit $\mathrm{M}$ phase and directly enter $\mathrm{G}_0$ phase.
They arrest their cell cycle permanently in the $\mathrm{G}_2$ phase.
They exit $\mathrm{S}$ phase and enter a quiescent stage.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, some cells in adult animals do not appear to exhibit division (e.g., heart cells) and many other cells divide only occasionally. These cells that do not divide further exit the $\mathrm{G}_1$ phase to enter an inactive stage called the quiescent stage ($\mathrm{G}_0$) of the cell cycle.

A common misconception is that cells exit the $\mathrm{M}$ phase directly to enter $\mathrm{G}_0$, but the transition specifically occurs by exiting the $\mathrm{G}_1$ phase.

Answer: They exit $\mathrm{G}_1$ phase to enter an inactive stage called $\mathrm{G}_0$.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In animal cells, the centriole duplicates in the nucleus during the S phase.
Reason (R): During the S phase, the amount of DNA per cell doubles in the nucleus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct
questions.solution:
The Assertion is incorrect because in animal cells, the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm, not the nucleus, during the S phase.

The Reason is correct because the S phase (Synthesis phase) marks the period during which DNA replication occurs, leading to a doubling of the DNA content per cell within the nucleus.

Therefore, the Assertion is incorrect but the Reason is correct.

Answer: Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During the pachytene stage of meiosis I, recombination nodules appear on the bivalents.
Reason (R): Recombination nodules represent the sites where crossing over occurs between sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: During the pachytene stage of prophase I in meiosis I, the bivalent chromosomes clearly appear as tetrads and this stage is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules.

Reason (R) is false: Recombination nodules represent the sites where crossing over occurs, but crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, not sister chromatids. A common mistake is failing to distinguish between sister and non-sister chromatids; exchange between sister chromatids would not result in genetic recombination.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During a specific stage of meiosis, the exchange of genetic material actively occurs between the non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes. Which specific morphological structure marks the exact site where this exchange takes place?
questions.solution:
The exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes is a process known as crossing over.

According to NCERT, crossing over occurs during the pachytene stage of prophase I. This stage is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, which are the specific morphological structures that mark the exact sites where crossing over takes place.

The synaptonemal complex is a protein scaffold formed earlier during zygotene to pair homologous chromosomes. Chiasmata are X-shaped structures that become visible later during diplotene when the synaptonemal complex dissolves. Kinetochores are disc-shaped structures at the centromere that serve as attachment sites for spindle fibres.

Answer: Recombination nodule

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During the pachytene stage of prophase I, recombination nodules appear on the bivalents to mark the sites of crossing over. Which of the following correctly describes the nature of this crossing over process?
options: It is a non-enzymatic physical breakage and reunion of chromatids.
It is an enzyme-mediated process primarily involving the enzyme recombinase.
It is an enzyme-mediated process primarily involving DNA ligase only.
It is an enzyme-mediated process primarily involving RNA polymerase.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, crossing over occurs during the pachytene stage of prophase I in meiosis. It is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, which mark the sites where the exchange of genetic material takes place between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

Crossing over is strictly an enzyme-mediated process. The specific enzyme complex involved in this recombination process is called recombinase. It does not occur through mere physical breakage without enzymes, nor are DNA ligase or RNA polymerase the primary enzymes characterising this event.

Answer: It is an enzyme-mediated process primarily involving the enzyme recombinase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In mitotic anaphase, centromeres split and sister chromatids separate, whereas in anaphase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes separate but centromeres do not split.
Reason (R): Mitosis is characterized as an equational division, whereas meiosis I is a reductional division.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Both statements are factually correct according to NCERT.

In mitotic anaphase, the splitting of centromeres allows sister chromatids to separate, which maintains the chromosome number in the daughter cells. In anaphase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres, which halves the chromosome number.

The mechanical events of chromosome separation described in the Assertion are the underlying cause for the division being equational or reductional as described in the Reason. Because the Reason states the outcome rather than the cause, it does not explain the Assertion. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During a specific phase of mitosis, the spindle fibres pull the sister chromatids towards the opposite poles of the cell. Which of the following events does NOT occur during this phase?
options: Chromosomes decondense and lose their individuality
Movement of chromatids to opposite poles
questions.solution:
The phase described in the question, where spindle fibres pull chromatids to opposite poles, is anaphase.

The key events of anaphase are the splitting of centromeres, separation of chromatids, and their movement to opposite poles.

The decondensation of chromosomes and the loss of their individuality is a characteristic event of telophase, which follows anaphase.

Answer: Chromosomes decondense and lose their individuality

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During meiosis I, the complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent. In which stage of prophase I do the four chromatids of each bivalent become distinct and clearly appear as tetrads?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, during the zygotene stage, homologous chromosomes start pairing together to form bivalents. However, these bivalents are not clearly visible at this stage.

The first two stages of prophase I (leptotene and zygotene) are relatively short-lived compared to the next stage, which is pachytene. During the pachytene stage, the four chromatids of each bivalent chromosome become distinct and clearly appear as tetrads. Students often confuse the formation of bivalents (zygotene) with their clear visibility as tetrads (pachytene).

Answer: Pachytene

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Some cells in adult animals, such as heart cells, do not exhibit division and enter an inactive stage called the quiescent stage ($\text{G}_{0}$). Which of the following correctly describes the phase they exit to enter $\text{G}_{0}$ and their metabolic status during this stage?
options: They exit the $\text{G}_{1}$ phase and remain metabolically active.
They exit the $\text{G}_{1}$ phase and become metabolically inactive.
They exit the $\text{G}_{2}$ phase and remain metabolically active.
They exit the $\text{S}$ phase and become metabolically inactive.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, cells that do not divide further (such as heart cells) exit the $\text{G}_{1}$ phase to enter an inactive stage called the quiescent stage ($\text{G}_{0}$) of the cell cycle.

Although it is termed an inactive stage regarding cell proliferation, the cells in this stage remain metabolically active. They simply no longer proliferate unless called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism. Therefore, they exit $\text{G}_{1}$ and remain metabolically active.

Answer: They exit the $\text{G}_{1}$ phase and remain metabolically active.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A researcher observes two animal cells, Cell X and Cell Y, and records the following parameters:

Cell X: Metabolically active, non-proliferating, DNA content is 2C, and possesses a single centrosome.
Cell Y: Metabolically active, possesses an intact nuclear envelope, DNA content is 4C, and has two centrosomes in the cytoplasm.

Identify the most likely cell cycle phases of Cell X and Cell Y respectively.
options: Cell X: G_{0}$ phase; Cell Y: G_{2}$ phase
Cell X: $G_{1}$ phase; Cell Y: M phase
Cell X: G_{0}$ phase; Cell Y: G_{1}$ phase
Cell X: $G_{2}$ phase; Cell Y: S phase
questions.solution:
Cell X has a DNA content of 2C and a single centrosome, indicating it has not undergone the S phase. Since it is non-proliferating but metabolically active, it is in the quiescent stage or G_{0}$ phase. \\ \\ Cell Y has a DNA content of 4C and two centrosomes, indicating it has successfully completed the S phase where DNA replication and centrosome duplication occur. The presence of an intact nuclear envelope confirms it is still in interphase and has not entered the M phase (where the nuclear envelope disintegrates). Thus, Cell Y is in the G_{2}$ phase.

Therefore, Cell X is in the G_{0}$ phase and Cell Y is in the G_{2}$ phase.

Answer: Cell X: G_{0}$ phase; Cell Y: G_{2}$ phase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the quiescent stage ($\mathrm{G}_0$) of the cell cycle:

(I) Cells that do not divide further exit $\mathrm{G}_1$ phase to enter the $\mathrm{G}_0$ phase.
(II) Cells in the $\mathrm{G}_0$ phase are metabolically inactive.
(III) Heart cells in adult animals are an example of cells that enter the $\mathrm{G}_0$ phase.
(IV) Cells in the $\mathrm{G}_0$ phase can never proliferate again under any circumstances.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, cells that do not divide further exit the $\mathrm{G}_1$ phase to enter an inactive stage called the quiescent stage ($\mathrm{G}_0$). Thus, statement (I) is correct.

Cells in this stage remain metabolically active, making statement (II) incorrect.

Heart cells in adult animals do not exhibit division and are a classic example of cells in the $\mathrm{G}_0$ phase, so statement (III) is correct.

These cells no longer proliferate unless called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism. Therefore, they can divide again under specific conditions, making statement (IV) incorrect.

Since only statements (I) and (III) are correct, a total of two statements are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II:

List IList II
A. DiakinesisI. Resembles normal mitosis
B. PachyteneII. Reductional division
C. Meiosis IIII. Chromosomes are fully condensed
D. Meiosis IIIV. Recombination nodules appear

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, during diakinesis, the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled. Pachytene is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes. Meiosis I is a reductional division where homologous chromosomes separate, reducing the chromosome number to half. Meiosis II is an equational division that resembles normal mitosis, where sister chromatids separate.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A biologist observes a dividing cell under a microscope and notes that the synaptonemal complex has dissolved. The recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents have separated from each other, except at specific X-shaped regions where they remain attached.

Identify the stage of cell division this cell will enter NEXT, along with the primary event that characterizes it.
options: Diplotene; Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex
Pachytene; Crossing over between non-sister chromatids
Diakinesis; Formation of the synaptonemal complex
questions.solution:
The cell described is currently in the diplotene stage of prophase I. This stage is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of recombined homologous chromosomes to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers (forming X-shaped chiasmata).

The question asks for the stage the cell will enter NEXT. The stage following diplotene is diakinesis.

Diakinesis is characterised by the terminalisation of chiasmata, where the chiasmata move towards the ends of the chromosomes.

Answer: Diakinesis; Terminalisation of chiasmata

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following cellular events:
I. Formation of synaptonemal complex
II. Splitting of centromere
III. Formation of recombination nodules
IV. Alignment of bivalents on the equatorial plate
V. Attachment of spindle fibres to kinetochores

How many of the above events occur exclusively during meiosis and are never observed in mitosis?
questions.solution:
Let us evaluate each event:

I. Formation of synaptonemal complex occurs during zygotene of Prophase I in meiosis. It is absent in mitosis.

II. Splitting of centromere occurs during anaphase of mitosis and anaphase II of meiosis. It is not exclusive to meiosis.

III. Formation of recombination nodules occurs during pachytene of Prophase I in meiosis. It is absent in mitosis.

IV. Alignment of bivalents on the equatorial plate occurs during metaphase I of meiosis. In mitosis, individual chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, not bivalents.

V. Attachment of spindle fibres to kinetochores occurs in both mitosis and meiosis.

Thus, exactly three events (I, III, and IV) are exclusive to meiosis.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cells in the $G_{0}$ phase of the cell cycle do not proliferate but remain metabolically active.
Reason (R): Cells that do not divide further exit the S phase to enter an inactive stage called the quiescent stage.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because cells in the $G_{0}$ (quiescent) stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism. \\ \\ Reason (R) is false because according to NCERT, cells that do not divide further exit the G_{1}$ phase (not the S phase) to enter the inactive stage called the quiescent stage (G_{0}$) of the cell cycle.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Some cells in adult animals do not appear to exhibit division (e.g., heart cells) and enter an inactive stage called the quiescent stage ($G_{0}$). Which specific phase of the standard cell cycle do these cells exit to enter the $G_{0}$ phase?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, cells that do not divide further exit the $G_{1}$ phase to enter an inactive stage called the quiescent stage ($G_{0}$) of the cell cycle.

These cells remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism. Therefore, the correct exit point from the standard cell cycle is the $G_{1}$ phase.

Answer: $G_{1}$ phase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following cellular events carefully:
X: Centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm of animal cells.
Y: Proteins are synthesized in preparation for mitosis.
Z: Cells remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so.

Identify the cell cycle phases corresponding to the events X, Y, and Z respectively.
options: X - $G_2$ phase, Y - S phase, Z - $G_1$ phase
X - S phase, Y - $G_1$ phase, Z - $G_0$ phase
X - S phase, Y - $G_2$ phase, Z - $G_0$ phase
X - $G_1$ phase, Y - $G_2$ phase, Z - $G_0$ phase
questions.solution:
Event X corresponds to the S phase (synthesis phase). During this phase, DNA replication occurs in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm of animal cells.

Event Y corresponds to the $G_2$ phase. During the $G_2$ phase, proteins are synthesized in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.

Event Z corresponds to the $G_0$ phase (quiescent stage). Cells in this stage exit the $G_1$ phase and enter an inactive stage where they do not proliferate but remain metabolically active.

Answer: X - S phase, Y - $G_2$ phase, Z - $G_0$ phase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The X-shaped structures called chiasmata become visible during the diplotene stage of meiosis I.

Reason (R): Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex occurs during diplotene, causing recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the beginning of diplotene is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers. These X-shaped structures are called chiasmata.

Thus, the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex is the direct mechanical cause that allows the homologous chromosomes to pull apart, making the chiasmata (the points of attachment where crossing over occurred) clearly visible.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation for (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During mitosis, spindle fibres attach to specific small disc-shaped structures present on the surface of the primary constriction of chromosomes. Identify these structures.
questions.solution:
Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores. These structures serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres to the chromosomes during cell division.

The centromere is the primary constriction itself, not the disc-shaped attachment site. The centrosome is the organelle that organizes the spindle fibres, and chromatids are the longitudinal halves of a replicated chromosome.

Answer: Kinetochores

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A diploid cell in the $\text{G}_{1}$ phase of its cell cycle has $14$ chromosomes and a DNA content of $2\text{C}$. Match the stages of the cell cycle in List-I with the corresponding number of chromosomes and DNA content in the cell in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) $\text{G}_{2}$ phase(i) $14$ chromosomes, $2\text{C}$ DNA
(B) Anaphase of mitosis(ii) $14$ chromosomes, $4\text{C}$ DNA
(C) Daughter cell after cytokinesis(iii) $28$ chromosomes, $4\text{C}$ DNA


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
In the $\text{G}_{1}$ phase, the cell has $14$ chromosomes and $2\text{C}$ DNA.

During the S phase, DNA replication occurs, doubling the DNA content to $4\text{C}$. However, the chromosome number remains the same because the sister chromatids are attached at a single centromere. Thus, in the $\text{G}_{2}$ phase, the cell has $14$ chromosomes and $4\text{C}$ DNA. This matches (A) with (ii).

During anaphase of mitosis, the centromeres split and sister chromatids separate. Each chromatid is now considered an individual chromosome. This temporarily doubles the chromosome number in the cell to $28$, while the total DNA content in the intact cell remains $4\text{C}$ (since the cell has not yet divided). This matches (B) with (iii).

After cytokinesis, the cell divides into two daughter cells, each receiving half the chromosomes and half the DNA. Each daughter cell will therefore have $14$ chromosomes and $2\text{C}$ DNA, restoring the $\text{G}_{1}$ state. This matches (C) with (i).

Answer: (A)-(ii), (B)-(iii), (C)-(i)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the S phase of the cell cycle:

(A) The amount of DNA per cell doubles from 2C to 4C during S phase.
(B) The chromosome number increases from 2n to 4n during S phase.
(C) In animal cells, the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm during S phase.
(D) DNA replication begins in the cytoplasm during S phase.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct: During the S phase, the amount of DNA per cell doubles (e.g., from 2C to 4C).

Statement (B) is incorrect: There is no increase in the chromosome number during the S phase; a diploid cell (2n) remains 2n.

Statement (C) is correct: In animal cells, centriole duplication occurs in the cytoplasm during the S phase.

Statement (D) is incorrect: DNA replication begins in the nucleus, not the cytoplasm.

Therefore, exactly two statements (A and C) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The amount of DNA per cell doubles during the synthesis (S) phase, but the chromosome number remains the same.

Reason (R): Karyokinesis strictly follows the G2 phase to ensure the equal distribution of the duplicated sister chromatids.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because during the S phase, DNA replication occurs, causing the DNA content to double (e.g., from 2C to 4C). However, the chromosome number remains unchanged because the newly formed sister chromatids remain attached at a single centromere.

Reason (R) is also correct as karyokinesis (nuclear division) occurs during the M phase, which follows the G2 phase, and it results in the separation and equal distribution of these chromatids.

However, (R) is not the correct explanation for (A). The chromosome number remains the same during the S phase due to the structural attachment of chromatids at the centromere, not because of the events of the subsequent karyokinesis.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Disruption of the mitotic spindle apparatus immediately after metaphase results in a cell with double the normal number of chromosomes.

Reason (R): The centromeres split and sister chromatids separate, but they fail to move to opposite poles due to the absence of spindle fibers.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. Disrupting the spindle apparatus after metaphase prevents the segregation of chromatids into two daughter cells, trapping all chromosomes in one cell and effectively doubling the chromosome number (inducing polyploidy).

Reason (R) is also true and correctly explains the Assertion. The splitting of centromeres and separation of sister chromatids is a biochemical event that occurs at the onset of anaphase. This splitting can occur even if spindle fibers are disrupted. However, without the spindle fibers to pull them, the separated chromatids (which are now considered individual chromosomes) cannot move to opposite poles. Thus, they remain in the same cell, leading to a doubled chromosome number.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the sub-stages of prophase I and their characteristic events.

List-IList-II
(A) Zygotene(I) Terminalisation of chiasmata
(B) Pachytene(II) Crossing over
(C) Diplotene(III) Synapsis
(D) Diakinesis(IV) Dissolution of synaptonemal complex

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Zygotene is characterized by the pairing of homologous chromosomes, a process called synapsis, which is accompanied by the formation of the synaptonemal complex. Hence, (A) matches with (III).

Pachytene is the stage where crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes. Hence, (B) matches with (II).

Diplotene is marked by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the appearance of chiasmata. Hence, (C) matches with (IV).

Diakinesis is the final stage of prophase I, marked by the terminalisation of chiasmata. Hence, (D) matches with (I).

Therefore, the correct matching sequence is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Arrange the following cytological events in the correct sequential order as they occur during Prophase I of meiosis:

A. Terminalisation of chiasmata
B. Appearance of recombination nodules
C. Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex
D. Formation of bivalents

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Formation of bivalents (D) occurs during the zygotene stage due to the synapsis of homologous chromosomes.

Appearance of recombination nodules (B) occurs during the pachytene stage, where crossing over takes place.

Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex (C) marks the beginning of the diplotene stage.

Terminalisation of chiasmata (A) is the defining event of diakinesis, the final stage of prophase I.

The correct chronological sequence of prophase I sub-stages is Zygotene → Pachytene → Diplotene → Diakinesis.

Therefore, the correct order of events is D, B, C, A.

Answer: D, B, C, A

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) Zygotene(I) Terminalisation of chiasmata
(B) Pachytene(II) Appearance of recombination nodules
(C) Diplotene(III) Formation of synaptonemal complex
(D) Diakinesis(IV) Appearance of X-shaped chiasmata

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
During Prophase-I of meiosis, different substages are characterised by specific cytological events:

Zygotene (A) is characterised by the pairing of homologous chromosomes (synapsis) and the formation of the synaptonemal complex (III).

Pachytene (B) is marked by the appearance of recombination nodules (II), which are the sites of crossing over.

Diplotene (C) begins with the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex, and the homologous chromosomes separate except at the sites of crossovers, forming X-shaped structures called chiasmata (IV).

Diakinesis (D) is the final stage of Prophase-I and is marked by the terminalisation of chiasmata (I).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres to the chromosomes during metaphase. These structures are called
questions.solution:
During metaphase, spindle fibres attach to the chromosomes. The specific sites of attachment are small disc-shaped structures present at the surface of the centromeres, which are known as kinetochores.

The centromere is the primary constriction of the chromosome, but the actual attachment points for the spindle microtubules are the kinetochores.

Centrosomes and centrioles are organelles that organise the spindle fibres at the poles of the cell, not the structures on the chromosomes where the fibres attach.

Answer: Kinetochores

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statement and choose the option that correctly fills the blanks.

In animal cells, the centriole duplicates in the ___(i)___ during the ___(ii)___ phase and begins to move towards opposite poles during the ___(iii)___ stage.
questions.solution:
In animal cells, during the S phase of interphase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus while the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm.

During Prophase, which is the first stage of mitosis, the duplicated centrioles (centrosomes) begin to move towards the opposite poles of the cell.

Therefore, the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm (i) during the S phase (ii) and begins to move towards opposite poles during the Prophase (iii) stage. Options suggesting the nucleus for centriole duplication confuse it with DNA replication, while those suggesting $G_2$ or Metaphase misidentify the timing of these key events.

Answer: (i) cytoplasm, (ii) S, (iii) Prophase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(i) Initiation of the assembly of mitotic spindle occurs in prophase.
(ii) Cells at the end of prophase, when viewed under the microscope, do not show Golgi complexes, endoplasmic reticulum, nucleolus and the nuclear envelope.
(iii) In telophase, chromosomes cluster at opposite spindle poles and their identity is lost as discrete elements.
(iv) During anaphase, the centromere of each chromosome is directed towards the equator while the arms trail behind.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (i) is correct as the initiation of the assembly of the mitotic spindle is a characteristic event of prophase.

Statement (ii) is correct because by the end of prophase, organelles like the Golgi complexes, endoplasmic reticulum, nucleolus, and the nuclear envelope disappear.

Statement (iii) is correct as telophase is marked by the decondensation of chromosomes at opposite poles, where they lose their individuality and discrete identity.

Statement (iv) is incorrect. During anaphase, as the chromosomes move away from the equatorial plate, the centromere of each chromosome is directed towards the pole (leading edge), while the arms trail behind.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During the diplotene stage of meiosis I, the recombined homologous chromosomes of a bivalent do not separate completely from each other.
Reason (R): The synaptonemal complex remains intact and stabilizes the bivalents throughout the diplotene stage.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
During the diplotene stage, the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents have a tendency to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers, forming X-shaped structures called chiasmata. Thus, they do not separate completely, making the Assertion true.

The beginning of the diplotene stage is recognized by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex, not its maintenance. Therefore, the Reason is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the cell cycle:

(I) The M phase represents the phase when the actual cell division or mitosis occurs.
(II) Interphase lasts for more than 95% of the duration of the cell cycle.
(III) During $\text{G}_{1}$ phase, the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA.
(IV) In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Based on the NCERT concepts of the cell cycle:

Statement (I) is correct: The M phase is the period of actual cell division or mitosis.

Statement (II) is correct: The interphase is the resting phase, which lasts for more than 95% of the total duration of the cell cycle.

Statement (III) is correct: During the $\text{G}_{1}$ phase, the cell is metabolically active and grows continuously but does not replicate its DNA.

Statement (IV) is correct: In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm.

Since all four statements are correct, the correct option is 'All four'.

Answer: All four

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The beginning of the diplotene stage of prophase I is recognized by the:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the beginning of diplotene is recognized by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers.

Formation of the synaptonemal complex occurs earlier, during the zygotene stage.

Appearance of recombination nodules is a characteristic feature of the pachytene stage.

Complete terminalisation of chiasmata marks diakinesis, the final stage of prophase I.

Answer: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the phases of mitosis and their key events:

List-IList-II
A. ProphaseI. Centromeres split and chromatids separate
B. MetaphaseII. Chromosomes align at the equator
C. AnaphaseIII. Initiation of condensation of chromosomal material
D. TelophaseIV. Nucleolus, Golgi complex and ER reform

Choose the correct matching from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the hallmark events of the mitotic phases are as follows:

Prophase is marked by the initiation of condensation of chromosomal material (A-III).

Metaphase is characterized by the alignment of chromosomes at the equator, forming the metaphase plate (B-II).

Anaphase is defined by the simultaneous splitting of centromeres and the separation of sister chromatids, which then migrate to opposite poles (C-I).

Telophase is the final stage where chromosomes decondense and lose their individuality, and organelles such as the nucleolus, Golgi complex, and ER reform (D-IV).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.

Answer: A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A student observes a meiotic cell where the nucleolus has disappeared and the nuclear envelope has completely broken down. This stage is immediately preceded by a specific phase of Prophase-I. Which of the following events is the primary characteristic of this preceding phase?
questions.solution:
The disappearance of the nucleolus and the breakdown of the nuclear envelope mark the end of diakinesis, the final stage of Prophase-I.

The stage that immediately precedes diakinesis is diplotene.

The primary characteristic of the diplotene stage is the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers, forming X-shaped structures called chiasmata.

Terminalisation of chiasmata occurs in diakinesis, appearance of recombination nodules occurs in pachytene, and the formation of the synaptonemal complex occurs in zygotene.

Answer: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The beginning of a particular stage of prophase I is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers. Identify the stage.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the beginning of diplotene is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers. These X-shaped structures are called chiasmata.

Zygotene is characterised by the formation of the synaptonemal complex and synapsis.

Pachytene is characterised by the occurrence of crossing over.

Diakinesis is marked by the terminalisation of chiasmata.

Answer: Diplotene

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Zygotene(I) Terminalisation of chiasmata
(B) Pachytene(II) Chiasmata formation
(C) Diplotene(III) Crossing over
(D) Diakinesis(IV) Synapsis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Zygotene is the second stage of prophase I, characterised by the pairing of homologous chromosomes, a process called synapsis.

Pachytene is the third stage, during which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

Diplotene is the fourth stage, marked by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the formation of X-shaped structures called chiasmata.

Diakinesis is the final stage of prophase I, marked by the terminalisation of chiasmata.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A meiocyte is observed at the $\text{G}_{1}$ phase with $20$ chromosomes and a DNA content of $2\text{C}$. What will be the chromosome number and DNA content per cell at the end of Meiosis I?
questions.solution:
In a meiocyte, the cell cycle begins with the $\text{G}_{1}$ phase where the chromosome number is $20$ ($2n$) and the DNA content is $2\text{C}$.

During the S phase, DNA replication occurs, doubling the DNA content to $4\text{C}$, while the chromosome number remains $20$.

Meiosis I is a reductional division where homologous chromosomes separate into two daughter cells. This halves the chromosome number to $10$ ($n$) per cell.

The total DNA content ($4\text{C}$) is also distributed equally between the two daughter cells, resulting in $2\text{C}$ of DNA per cell at the end of Meiosis I.

Answer: $10$ chromosomes and $2\text{C}$ DNA

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During prophase I of meiosis, the exchange of genetic material occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes. The specific sites where this process takes place are characterized by the appearance of:
questions.solution:
During the pachytene stage of prophase I, crossing over occurs, which is the exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

According to NCERT, the sites at which crossing over occurs are characterized by the appearance of recombination nodules.

Chiasmata are the X-shaped structures that become visible later during the diplotene stage as a consequence of crossing over. The synaptonemal complex is a protein structure formed during the earlier zygotene stage to mediate chromosome pairing. Kinetochores are disc-shaped structures present on the centromere for spindle fibre attachment.

Answer: Recombination nodules

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the sub-stages of Prophase I in meiosis:

(A)Zygotene(i)Terminalisation of chiasmata
(B)Pachytene(ii)Visibility of X-shaped chiasmata
(C)Diplotene(iii)Formation of synaptonemal complex
(D)Diakinesis(iv)Appearance of recombination nodules

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
During meiosis I, Prophase I is divided into five phases based on chromosomal behaviour.

Zygotene is characterised by the pairing of homologous chromosomes (synapsis) and the formation of the synaptonemal complex. (A matches iii)

Pachytene is the stage where crossing over occurs, marked by the appearance of recombination nodules. (B matches iv)

Diplotene is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the visibility of X-shaped structures called chiasmata. (C matches ii)

Diakinesis is the final stage of Prophase I, marked by the terminalisation of chiasmata. (D matches i)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(iii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(ii), (D)-(i).

Answer: (A)-(iii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(ii), (D)-(i)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In oocytes of some vertebrates, a specific stage of meiosis I can last for months or years. Identify this arrested stage and the specific structure that holds the homologous chromosomes together during this prolonged phase.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, in oocytes of some vertebrates, the diplotene stage can last for months or years.

During the beginning of diplotene, the synaptonemal complex dissolves. The recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents tend to separate from each other except at the sites of crossing over. These X-shaped structures where the chromosomes remain physically attached are called chiasmata.

Therefore, during this prolonged arrested phase, it is the chiasmata that hold the homologous chromosomes together, not the synaptonemal complex (which has already dissolved) or recombination nodules (which characterize pachytene).

Answer: Diplotene and Chiasmata

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A diploid animal cell with $2n = 16$ is undergoing meiosis. How many centromeres and chromatids, respectively, will be observed moving towards each pole during Anaphase I?
questions.solution:
During Anaphase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes separate and move towards opposite poles, but the centromeres do not split.

Since the diploid number is $2n = 16$, there are 16 chromosomes in total. During Anaphase I, half of the chromosomes (8 chromosomes) move to each pole.

Because the centromeres remain intact, each of these 8 chromosomes still consists of two sister chromatids. Therefore, there are 8 centromeres and $8 \times 2 = 16$ chromatids moving towards each pole.

Answer: 8 centromeres and 16 chromatids

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
